rv.q: George Bernard Shaw's 'Mrs. Warren's Profession' hasn't had a happy life.
This production feels like a polite drawing-room exercise, when it should crackle with the heat of moral and social indignation.
Unfortunately, it's nowhere to be seen in a production whose edges have all been dulled.
With so little going on, too many of the scenes feel endless.
But overall, a little nipping and tucking better blocked scenes, some trims of long-winded passages, warmer sets would have made this show's oftentimes arduous work a lot more appealing.
Ultimately, her accent undermines the entire enterprise and makes the revered actress’ return to the stage after several years a let-down.
Doug Hughes, the Roundabout Theater Company’s resident director, has put together a production that has two main draws

cn.t: Cherry Jones leads a competent but unexciting revival of Shaw's early work that feels like a polite drawing-room exercise when it should crackle with heat and urgency for modern audiences.

vs.sum: Completed a major renovation in early 2026 with all seats replaced and legroom expanded, making it one of Broadway's most comfortable and modern houses. New restrooms significantly reduce intermission wait times.

acc.note: Elevators to all levels. 53 assistive listening devices. 11 wheelchair seats across Orchestra and Balcony.
